title: A Capital Expenditure Straddling a New Approval Threshold
scenario_text:
A facilities operations manager at Juniperwell Logistics must decide who must approve a capital equipment purchase, given two prior decisions that straddle a threshold change.

**Decision A (2024-01-30)**
A $60K forklift purchase was approved by the site director alone. Note: 'Under the capex policy then in effect, site directors could approve capital purchases up to $75K without CFO sign-off. Within limit — approved by the director.'

**Decision B (2024-09-10)**
A $58K conveyor upgrade was routed for CFO approval. Note: 'Under the revised capex policy effective 2024-08-01, the site-director approval ceiling was lowered to $50K; anything above $50K now requires CFO sign-off. The $58K purchase was sent to the CFO.'

**Current request C (2024-12-12)**
A $62K pallet-racking system purchase is ready. The site director wants to approve it directly, pointing to the January forklift approval as the model.

**Capital Expenditure Policy (current, effective 2024-08-01)**
Site directors may approve capital purchases up to $50K. Capital purchases above $50K require CFO approval. The $50K site-director ceiling has been in force since August 1, 2024, replacing the prior $75K ceiling.

**Slack — #facilities-ops**
Director: 'I approved a $60K forklift on my own back in January, so I can approve this $62K racking the same way.'
Manager: 'January was under the old $75K ceiling. That dropped to $50K in August, and we already sent a $58K purchase to the CFO in September. Let me confirm the current path.'

The $62K purchase is above the current $50K site-director ceiling.
question: Under the current capex policy, whose approval is required for the $62K pallet-racking purchase? Provide the required approver.
